content.title: About
content.content: Coconut oil is extracted from the flesh of mature coconuts (Cocos nucifera). It has a distinctive aroma and a mild sweet taste. The oil is widely used in cooking, cosmetics, and traditional medicine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coconut oil contains about 90 % saturated fatty acids, most of which are lauric acid.
Traditionally, coconut oil has been used in tropical regions as a skin and hair care product.
In the 19th century, coconut oil was exported from Southeast Asia to Europe and the USA as “lamp oil”.
Coconut oil remains liquid above 24 °C and solidifies at lower temperatures.

items.title: Heart health support
items.content: Lauric acid may raise HDL (the “good”) cholesterol level.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Medium‑chain triglycerides are quickly metabolized and can serve as a rapid energy source.

items.title: Skin moisturization
items.content: It forms a protective barrier that helps retain moisture in the epidermis.

items.title: Hair care
items.content: Regular application can reduce dryness and brittleness of hair.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Vitamin E and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may contribute to elevated total cholesterol levels.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Coconut oil is very calorie‑dense (about 900 kcal per 100 g), so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Not suitable for high‑heat frying
items.content: Overheating can lead to the formation of trans fats and loss of beneficial properties.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use coconut oil for sautéing, baking, and adding to smoothies. In cosmetics, apply it to skin and hair as a moisturizing and nourishing treatment.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dark place. It stays liquid above 24 °C and solidifies below that temperature, but its qualities remain unchanged. Shelf life is typically 2‑3 years.
